items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: it was Freddie Davis’ repair shop, and I saw this great big beautiful silver ba— a Conn bass saxophone sitting on the mantle. I said to Freddie, I said, “Whose is that?”

ctx.x: Tony DeNicola is my favorite drummer because he really takes me home, and Greg Cohn is just a very intuitive, deeply rooted musician who’s heard and cares. Well the story I’ll tell you about, speaking of caring, I once drove to, when I was 16 years old, I drove to the Hotel New Yorker at 10:30 at night, parked my car on the street, which you could do then, painted in my moustache and drew up my double breasted suit and shirt and tie and I’m walking in the door and this goon who is standing at the door says, “Yeah…

this place and this goon is, “What do you want kid.” I said, “I want to see Mr. Rollini.” He looked at his watch and said, “Sit over there at that table, kid.” I said okay. I thought I could pass but obviously I failed. So anyway I’m sitting at the table and Rollini is just finishing up, six people in the joint. Six people.
